methods.sem_native: SEM-RRT* project reconstruction, C++ search engine (Python/scipy native raster as preprocessing), stops on convergence by the rule below, 20 s wall-clock cap, no iteration limit.
methods.a4_rpbit_l33_m20: Locked primary (lambda 33, M = 20 convergence batches, refinement on), unchanged since the lock of 2026-11-16T03:46:05.7959372Z; 20 s cap, self-stop on convergence.

sem_convergence_stop.definition: At every iteration boundary after the first solution: if the published native cost is below reference x (1 - relative_eps), it becomes the reference; otherwise, once window_iterations iterations have passed since the last reset, the search stops (termination CONVERGED_NO_IMPROVEMENT).
sem_convergence_stop.mirrors_a4: A4 applies the same test at batch boundaries with relative_eps 1e-3 and M = 20 batches; after the first solution a batch holds 200 samples, so its window is 4,000 samples. One SEM-RRT* iteration draws one sample.
sem_convergence_stop.implementation: SemRrtStar::setConvergenceStop (include/terrain25d/SemRrtStar.hpp, src/SemRrtStar.cpp), C ABI sem_set_convergence_stop / sem_convergence, tools/sem_native_cpp.py, request field sem_convergence_stop (tools/native_paper_worker.py, tools/rp_bit_protocol.py). Off by default: every earlier run is unchanged.
sem_convergence_stop.exact_prefix: The stop reads only the published cost (no random draw, no tree change), so a stopped search equals the same search without the stop cut at the same iteration. CTest group sem_native_cpp (test_convergence_stop_is_an_exact_prefix) checks this with == against both the C++ and the Python search.
sem_convergence_stop.validation: tools/rp_bit_validation.py: a SEM trial whose rule differs from the config is a correctness error (sem_convergence_stop_mismatch); a converged trial must have stopped exactly window_iterations after its last reference with a final cost in [reference x (1 - eps), reference] (else sem_convergence_inconsistent).

inputs.novelty: map seeds 81001-81010 and planner seeds 816001-816005 appear in no earlier config, tool, test, document or result directory (searched 2026-11-17)

timing_protocol: Kaggle CPU session (no accelerator). execution.cores [0]: one lane, one trial at a time, so the two methods never run concurrently.
One fresh process per trial, pinned to its lane core, one thread.
Both methods of a (map, planner seed) block run back to back on the same core; the method order alternates between blocks.

Solve clocks as in plan 5.3: A4 from before potential construction; SEM from planner construction, after loading the map and building the native raster and its C++ copy (reported separately as preprocessing). Time is each method's own stop.
gates_before_heldout: Linux build of the delivered sources; 31 CTest groups (as fairtime), sem_native_cpp now also checks the exact-prefix property of the stop.
smoke_selfstop: 7 smoke fixtures, 2 s, both methods; no correctness error, every A4 trial successful, strict validation.
gate_selfstop: the 5 families at map seed 51001, planner seed 516001, 20 s cap, both methods; same conditions.

sem_cpp_bit_identity: on the 5 gate_selfstop maps, planner seeds 516001 and 516002, Python and C++ SEM-RRT* (stop off) each run 7425 iterations and must be identical in status, counters and every incumbent (10/10), on the Linux runtime of the campaign.
Any failed gate stops the run before the held-out; the cause is reported, nothing is retuned.

primary_criteria.source: plan section 5.3, unchanged; evaluated by tools/analyze_rp_bit.py criteria() for a4_rpbit_l33_m20 against sem_native
items: PSR: A4 >= SEM, pooled and in every family.
Time: paired mean of (A4 solve time to its stop - SEM solve time to its stop) < 0.
J30 = L_H + 30 E / 40 by the independent oracle: paired mean difference < 0 and its one-sided upper 95% bound < 0 (hierarchical bootstrap map -> seed, 20000 replicates, seed 61016).
APL and PRI: pooled relative difference upper 95% bound < +1% (non-inferiority); target: pooled mean difference < 0.

secondary_descriptive: Termination reasons and stop times of both methods.
Anytime table at T in {0.5, 1, 2, 5, 10, 20} s (a stopped run keeps its last path).
A4 time to reach the final SEM-RRT* J30 of the same slot (tolerance 0 and 1%).
SEM-RRT* iterations per run; per-family tables and the failed attempts.
stated_expectation: On dev (local Windows) SEM-RRT* stopped on convergence in 75/75 runs (median 2.08 s, mean 2.83 s, max 10.1 s), A4 in 75/75 (mean 1.52 s); every criterion passed, but Time is the narrowest: A4 was faster in 51/75 pairs (mean -1.31 s). On Kaggle A4 slowed about 2.4x relative to Windows in the earlier runs while SEM-RRT* slowed about 1.4x, so the Time margin may shrink or reverse; J30 and STI are expected to stay in favour of A4. Every outcome is reported.
rules: Started trials are never retried; no seeds are added; criteria and analysis are not changed after any held-out result is seen.
Strict per-snapshot validation of the primary method; fast independent validation of every trial (including the stop rule).
Results are reported as measured on Kaggle Linux; their Time is not compared with Windows numbers.
limitations: Bit identity with the Python search is checked up to 7425 iterations; the stop is checked as an exact prefix of the C++ search.
Shared cloud VM: background load can add timing noise; both methods of a block share the core and alternate order.
The window is matched in samples, not in time or work: one BIT* sample and one SEM-RRT* iteration cost different amounts.
SEM-RRT* is the project reconstruction, not the authors code; the paper's own termination (5000 iterations) is not used.
